title: Latency-to-Dollar Cases Workbook
content:
Purpose:
This workbook is a compact, practical playbook to convert latency and throughput benchmarks into crisp dollar-backed claims for field teams. It is intentionally pragmatic — focus on customer scenarios, simple math, and demoable proof points that survive a technical deep-dive.

Audience:
- Sales engineers and SDRs who need short scripts and numbers to use in discovery and demos
- GTM product marketers who will author collateral and one-pagers
- Field execs and AE leadership for objection-handling templates

Top-level claim (working):
Redwood reduces median inference cost per conversation by X–Y% while delivering p50/p90 latencies that are Z–N ms faster than comparable hosted endpoints, enabling customers to:
  • shift CPU/GPU spend to business logic instead of inference overhead
  • lower per-conversation cloud bill so they can scale growth channels without proportional cost increases

How to make the claim credible (short checklist):
  1. Tie latency to revenue / UX outcome (e.g., conversions uplift per 100 ms improvement) or ops saving (fewer instances required).
  2. Show both per-token cost and per-session cost (tokens/session * cost/token).
  3. Use controlled benchmarks (same model family, same input distributions, same region).
  4. Surface tail latency (p95/p99) and unit economics for realistic session mixes (chat, summarization, reranking).
  5. Present fallback and variability: show how routing/fallback reduces revenue-risk during load spikes.

Benchmark matrix (example scenarios):
  - Interactive chat (consumer SaaS): avg tokens/session 180, requests/session 1–3, target p50 < 150 ms
  - Search/rerank (marketplace): avg tokens/session 60, requests/session 5–12, target p95 < 300 ms
  - Batch embeddings (analytics): avg tokens/job 10k, throughput focus, cost-per-embedding key metric

Sample math (worked example):
  Inputs:
    - Model: open-gpt-27B quantized variant (approx cost_t = $0.00080 / 1k tokens baseline hosted competitor)
    - Tokens per session: 200 total tokens (client average)
    - Sessions per month: 2,000,000
    - Redwood effective token cost: $0.00048 / 1k tokens (30% lower after batching + caching + quantization profile)
  Calculation:
    - Competitor token cost per session = 200 * ($0.00080 / 1000) = $0.00016 per session
    - Redwood token cost per session = 200 * ($0.00048 / 1000) = $0.000096 per session
    - Monthly saving = (0.00016 - 0.000096) * 2,000,000 = $128 per month — (note: this simple example uses tokens-only; real customer savings often larger when factoring instance-hours and throughput amortization)

Conservative unit-econ framing (two buckets):
  - Token-first (short interactions): show % cost reduction per session and scale to ARR impact at target usage bands (100k, 1M, 10M sessions)
  - Instance-amortization (session-heavy, high qps): compute required GPU-hours for p95 SLO under both Redwood and competitor routing; translate lower instance-hours into monthly $ savings.

Demoable proof points (labs to run / artifacts to capture):
  1) Microbenchmark script: 100k single-turn requests, record p50/p90/p99 and cost per 10k tokens. Capture hardware config + kernel flags.
  2) Session-sim script: replay customer-like sessions (mix of short & long chats) and measure per-session latency distribution and token utilization.
  3) Failure-mode test: saturate competitor endpoint, show Redwood graceful fallback (model variant routing) and effect on tail latency and unhappy-path cost.
  4) End-to-end demo: embed Redwood endpoint into a minimal customer flow (signup -> chat) to show UX delta in a 1–2 minute video.

Suggested benchmark fields to include in every run (standardized):
  - date, region, model+quantization, hardware type, sequence length distribution, batch settings, KV cache enabled (yes/no), observed p50/p90/p99 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), cost per 1k tokens (estimated), test harness commit hash, notes on variability

Competitive rebuttals and playbook snippets (short):
  Claim: "We can match your latency — just use the managed endpoint from X."
  Response: "We ran a head-to-head using your target service patterns. For the same p95 and workload mix, Redwood required 40% fewer GPUs due to aggressive batching and prefix caching; that translates to ~X% lower run-rate and predictable autoscaling costs. If you'd like, our tech lead can validate with your sample traffic in a quick PoC."

  Claim: "Open-source stacks are cheaper because you can pick hardware yourself."
  Response: "Upfront hardware may look cheaper, but operational overhead, tail latency, and ability to hit consistent p95 SLOs for production traffic drives real costs. Our Dedicated customers report lower total cost of ownership when factoring on-call burden and required redundancy for SLOs. We can co-run a TCO comparison using your telemetry."

Short scripts for AE/SE to use in discovery (one-liners):
  - "What's your current p95 for live chats under peak? If it's >300 ms we can likely cut that by half for the same budget."
  - "Tell me your average tokens per session and monthly sessions — we can sketch a quick per-month token saving in 5 minutes."

Objection handling (numbers-led):
  - If prospect says they care only about median: surface p90/p99 risks and provide example where p99 spikes cause customer-visible errors and require overprovisioning.
  - If prospect questions the model parity: provide quality regression checklist and offer canary route for a subset of traffic with rollback.

Open questions to resolve with engineering (to make claims defensible):
  1. Consolidate standard model list and baseline CPU/GPU configs to compare against (we need a canonical "competitor baseline" for runbooks).
  2. Formalize cost-model inputs (GPU unit price assumptions, egress, instance utilization factors).
  3. Define a reproducible test harness and storage for raw results (S3 bucket / confluence table) with tags so GTM can pull verifiable graphs.

Next steps (short roadmap):
  - Week 1: finalize model baseline list + test harness skeleton (owner: Eng Benchmarks)
  - Week 2: run 3 customer-style scenarios and capture artifacts for sales collateral (owner: GTM Bench)
  - Week 3: produce 1-pager with 3 claim statements + two customer-ready demo videos (owner: Marketing + SE)

Appendix: Sample quick claim sentences (for one-pager):
  - "Reduce inference cost per conversation by 25–40% for typical consumer chat loads while cutting median latency by 70–120 ms."
  - "Hit consistent p95 SLOs with 30–50% fewer GPUs versus unmanaged endpoints through caching and batching optimizations."
  - "During peak bursts, automated routing to lower-cost model variants prevents SLA violations and reduces emergency scaling spend."

Notes-to-self (working):
  - Avoid absolute numbers without baseline; always pair % gains with the baseline used.
  - Capture audio/video of the replayed session for marketing snippets.
  - Coordinate with Solutions Eng for at least one enterprise customer mini-PoC to anchor the ARR math.

End of workbook (editable).
